assessment.nobel_worthiness: Incretin physiology and GLP-1 receptor agonism span basic hormone biology through to therapies that have transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity care and are showing cardiovascular and renal benefit. The chain from discovery to a clearly transformative clinical outcome is unusually complete, and the impact is broad and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and secretion of GLP-1), Drucker (GLP-1 biology, receptor signalling, therapeutic rationale) and Mojsov (peptide chemistry identifying the active form) form a coherent basic-science trio. Knudsen's industrial development is decisive for the drugs but a three-person limit forces a choice, and Habener is not credited on this list; the allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple large randomized trials and wide clinical deployment over roughly two decades. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue given the scale of impact.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among Drucker, Holst, Mojsov, Knudsen (and uncredited Habener) is disputed and cannot all fit in three places.
Long-term safety and durability of effects are still being characterised, though this is unlikely to affect the prize case.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience a general method to control defined cell populations with light, enabling causal dissection of circuits and behaviour across species. The tool is originally conceived, conceptually clear and has become ubiquitous in biomedical research.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery and characterisation (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) and its neuronal deployment (Boyden, Deisseroth, and earlier Miesenboeck's genetically targeted photoactivation) are distributed across six credited people. Any three-person configuration leaves out major contributors, which is the principal obstacle.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than fifteen years of independent adoption, with clinical translation emerging in retinal vision restoration. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Priority and credit between the discovery of channelrhodopsin and its neuronal use is contested; Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck would be excluded.
Clinical impact is early; the case rests mainly on research-tool impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splice-modulating antisense oligonucleotide therapy for spinal muscular atrophy converted a fatal infantile disease into a treatable one. It combines mechanistic RNA-splicing insight with a drug platform and is a clear example of molecular understanding leading to clinical benefit.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (mechanistic identification of SMN2 exon 7 splicing control and ASO design) and Bennett (oligonucleotide chemistry and drug development with Ionis) provide a tidy two-person configuration. Other contributors in the original SMN2 splicing work (e.g. academic collaborators) are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature: approval of nusinersen in 2016 and years of long-term follow-up. The platform effect on other ASO therapies adds to its significance.
uncertainties: Some of the foundational splicing and SMN2 work involved other groups whose roles I cannot verify from this list.
Competition with gene therapy for SMA may shape how the committee frames the contribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered CAR-T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and established a new class of living cell therapies. The concept is original and has yielded multiple approved products with substantial survival benefit.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical translation of CD19/4-1BB CAR-T), Sadelain (CD28 co-stimulated CAR design and preclinical work) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early CAR trials) is a plausible trio. Eshhar and others who conceived the first-generation CAR are not credited here, which weakens the attribution.
assessment.maturity: Mature for haematologic cancers with long follow-up; limited efficacy in solid tumours and safety issues such as cytokine release and secondary malignancy remain.
uncertainties: Foundational concept attribution (first-generation chimeric receptors) is incomplete in the supplied credit.
Scope of benefit and toxicity profile are still evolving.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new intracellular signalling logic from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus, with wide relevance to secretory physiology, neurodegeneration, diabetes and cancer. It is a conceptually clean and highly original discovery.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently identified the core machinery (Ire1 and Hac1/XBP1 splicing, and the Ire1 signalling pathway), making a natural two-person prize; Ron and Walter on PERK would be potential additions but are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Mature and extensively confirmed from yeast to mammals over three decades. Therapeutic exploitation is still limited, so clinical impact is less direct than for other candidates.
uncertainties: Whether the committee requires clearer medical translation for a basic cell biology discovery.
Other contributors such as Ron are not in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Lgr5-based adult stem-cell organoid culture created a widely adopted platform for modelling epithelial biology, cancer and infection and for patient-derived testing. The principle is original and has generated a large field.
assessment.attribution: Clevers (Lgr5 stem cell identification and organoid concept) and Sato (the culture system as first author and developer) give a defensible pair. Credit for the broader organoid field, including pluripotent-derived organoids (Sasai, Lancaster, Knoblich), sits outside this entry.
assessment.maturity: Maturity is moderate: strong independent replication of the platform, but clinical translation and standardisation are still developing.
uncertainties: Overlap and potential priority issues with pluripotent stem-cell derived organoid work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway revealed how cytosolic DNA is sensed by innate immunity, with consequences for infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies and cancer immunology. It is a mechanistically elegant and conceptually new discovery.
assessment.attribution: Chen (cGAS and cGAMP as second messenger) and Barber (STING) are the two central figures; Ishikawa, Sun and Wu are co-discoverers in the primary papers but would be excluded by the three-name cap, and I choose two names to preserve a clean configuration.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is solid and widely confirmed; therapeutic application (STING agonists and inhibitors) has not yet delivered an approved drug, so the clinical case is still immature.
uncertainties: Absence of an approved therapy may count against timeliness.
Credit boundaries between STING discovery by multiple groups are not fully resolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR was identified as a central regulator of cell growth and nutrient sensing, connecting nutrient signals to growth control and informing therapy in transplantation and oncology via rapamycin analogues. The discovery is broad and conceptually important.
assessment.attribution: Hall (TOR genes and function) and Schreiber (chemical-genetic identification of the FKBP12-rapamycin target) form a defensible core. I leave out Sabatini given the listed ties to the later mTORC1 work and my uncertainty about how the committee should treat the contested aspects of his record; I cannot verify the details independently.
assessment.maturity: Mature with extensive confirmation and clinical use of rapalogs; the broader therapeutic promise in ageing and metabolism is still uncertain.
uncertainties: Relative weighting of Hall's TOR discovery versus Brown, Sabatini and others for rapamycin target identification and mTOR complexes.
Sabatini-related concerns are not independently verified by me.
